transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-07-08 16:00 PDT
- Duration: 48 minutes
- Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Anita (CTO, Sunridge), Marcus (ML Eng), Priya (Infra)

Summary:
Sunridge is evaluating whether to run Redwood hosted for initial integration versus Dedicated/Private for production. Primary concerns: multilingual support (English + three EMEA languages + Hindi), long-context retrieval (20k token-ish threads for case histories), tool-calling to internal search and RAG with external connectors, and strict KMS + VPC requirements. They want cost/latency trade-offs and a runbook for benchmarking.

Topics: open-model comparisons, context length & KV cache, multilingual eval, tool-calling and connectors, hosted vs dedicated vs private operational constraints, security/KMS/VPC, benchmarks and pilot next steps.

[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro, I'm Maya, AE on this account, and Diego's our solutions engineer. Anita, want to kick us off with what you're trying to solve?

[00:12] Anita (Sunridge): Sure. We run customer support automation across EU/UK/IN regions. Our use case needs a model that can keep about 15–20k tokens of context — customer history + docs — and we also need tool-calling into our search and an internal ticketing system. We're weighing managed hosted versus something more private for compliance.

[00:28] Diego (Redwood SE): Great, thanks. When you say 15–20k, is that sliding window or single-turn context for generation?

[00:34] Marcus (Sunridge): It's mostly cumulative — the conversation plus a few long-ticket attachments so in practice some turns hit 18–20k. We don't want to truncate important earlier notes.

[00:42] Diego: Okay. Two immediate things — model selection (open models with native long-context support vs shorter context + RAG) and ops (how we manage KV caching, batching, and routing). For ops, we recommend either Redwood Hosted with our long-context variants for initial dev, then Dedicated or Private if you need VPC/KMS and SLA.

[01:05] Priya (Infra): Our security team will require KMS/HSM for keys, VPC peering or private link, audit logs, and data residency in the EU for EU customers. Is that all supported on Hosted?

[01:13] Maya: Hosted supports SOC 2 and you can request region-specific deployments, but for customer-managed keys and full VPC isolation we usually steer enterprise customers to Dedicated or Private. We'll send the SOC2 pack.

[01:25] Anita: Good. On models — we're leaning open-source because of auditability. What are the good open-model options for long context and multilinguality?

[01:33] Diego: Right now, practical picks are: Llama2/3 variants (good base but need to check long-context forks), Mistral mixes, and specialized long-context models like LongForm-llm (vendor names sometimes vary in papers). There's also a newer set of dense+retriever hybrid models that allow shorter model context with RAG; that reduces cost but adds complexity. For multilingual, some open models degrade on low-resource languages. We typically recommend a hybrid approach: 8k/16k context LLM for short flows and RAG + retrieval for full 20k+ history.

[02:05] Marcus: The RAG approach could complicate the ticketing tool-calls — we'd need consistent deterministic outputs and tool-call reliability. How do you handle tool-calling in your hosted offering?

[02:14] Diego: We support function-style tool-calling / structured output. For Hosted, you can register connectors or call webhooks; for Dedicated/Private, you can run connectors inside your VPC so calls never leave your network. There's also a fallback pattern — model attempts tool-call, if tool unavailable we have deterministic fallback heuristics.

[02:34] Anita: What about the KV cache — is that the same as your prefix cache? We have older notes that say 'KVcash' somewhere in our docs which was confusing.

[02:40] Diego: (laughs) Yeah, KV cache — we've seen 'KVcash' in transcriptions before. The KV cache is the key-value attention cache; for long-context you can either store tokens as part of the model's context or use Golden-KV caching where repeated prefixes are cached across requests. That reduces token compute and cost. On Redwood Dedicated we let you tune eviction policies, chunking sizes, and offload to NVMe to extend effective context.

[03:05] Priya: If we go Dedicated or Private, can we bring our own KMS and HSM?

[03:10] Maya: Yes. Private supports customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations. Dedicated supports KMS via customer-managed keys in most cases — we'll include the integration notes in the security pack.

[03:23] Marcus: Latency is a big deal for us — sub-300ms p95 for short prompts and under 1.2s for longer completions. Are those numbers realistic?

[03:33] Diego: For hosted inference, short prompts to smaller open models can hit low-latency (200–300ms p95) if you pick smaller quantized variants, but longer contexts and larger models jump latency. Dedicated GPUs with pinned model sharding help. There's a trade-off: smaller quantized models lower cost and latency but may reduce accuracy on multilingual and complex reasoning. Our Optimize tooling can propose batching and quantization settings per workload.

[03:58] Anita: Can you walk through an example config for 20k context with tool-calling and our security constraints?

[04:05] Diego: Sure. Example: Private deployment in EU region with a long-context model compiled for 16–32k tokens (we'll test the 20k path), KV cache enabled with a 48-hour prefix retention for reuse, model quantized to 4-bit where feasible, and a local retriever that pre-selects relevant docs into the context — that keeps the model input smaller. Tool-calls are executed via a local connector that exposes an internal endpoint over mTLS. We can also do dedupe and prompt engineering to reduce token blow-up.

[04:36] Priya: About the retriever — will it be in our VPC?

[04:39] Diego: Yes, for Private or Dedicated the retriever and vector DB can be in your VPC. For Hosted we provide a managed vector store with region controls, but that means some data flows through Redwood-managed infra.

[04:52] Marcus: For multilingual benchmarks, any recommended test approach? We have English + German + French + Hindi.

[04:58] Diego: We usually run a two-stage eval: 1) intrinsic — token-level perplexity and BLEU-style checks on heldout; 2) extrinsic — run your actual prompts and measure correctness, hallucination, and tool-call accuracy. For Hindi and other lower-resource languages we add domain-specific fine-tuning or adapters; sometimes a multilingual retriever plus English-anchored summarization works well. We'll propose a benchmark matrix.

[05:28] Anita: Cost — can you ballpark hosted vs dedicated for our expected throughput? We're early stage, maybe 50k tokens/day rising to 1–2M tokens/day in Q4.

[05:38] Maya: Ballparks vary by model. Hosted with medium-sized open model might be lowest start-up cost; Dedicated will have base monthly reserved costs but better unit economics at scale. We will send a pricing sketch after we get your prompt mix.

[05:51] Marcus: One question re: determinism — our compliance needs reproducible outputs for audits. Do you support deterministic seeds and sticky model versions?

[05:59] Diego: Yes — you can pin model versions, set deterministic sampling, and we capture token-level audit logs for requests (subject to deployment type and retention policy). Private deployment gives you full control of logs.

[06:12] Anita: Any wildcard risks — proprietary vector DB, or vendor lock?

[06:17] Maya: We try to avoid lock-in; you can export embeddings and vectors, and we document expected formats. If you want on-prem vector DB we can integrate.

[06:26] Marcus: For the benchmark, can Diego propose two configurations: one hosted using a 16k context open model with RAG fallback, and one dedicated/private with 20k+ context model and KV cache tuned?

[06:34] Diego: Yep — I'll propose both and include expected p95/p99 and cost per 1k tokens estimates.

[06:41] Anita: About function/tool-calling reliability — we will have synchronous calls to internal search and async ticket creation. Is there retry/backoff that Redwood suggests?

[06:49] Diego: We recommend idempotent tool endpoints, a request-replay queue for async tool-calls, and a policy to convert failed tool-call into a safe fallback message. On Dedicated/Private you can host the connector inside the VPC to minimize network failure.

[07:05] Priya: A couple of practical questions — can you run inference on our own GPU fleet? We have spare A10s on a colo that we could dedicate.

[07:13] Maya: For Private, there's an on-prem package where you run our control plane and serving runtime; it supports common GPUs. We'll need to validate compatibility (driver versions, CUDA). Diego will follow up on ops checklist.

[07:24] Marcus: Are there limits on tool-calling per minute, or rate limiting by default?

[07:29] Diego: Hosted has rate limits and quotas that we can configure; Dedicated gives you higher throughput with reserved capacity. We'll map expected QPS to pool size.

[07:38] Anita: Anything surprising about multilingual tokenization? We had a prior issue: some languages exploded token counts.

[07:44] Diego: Yes — tokenization can cause surprises especially for agglutinative languages. For Hindi and some EU dialects we recommend measuring tokenizer overhead and perhaps using sentence-level chunking + summarization to compress context. Also consider using language-specific adapters.

[07:58] Marcus: Do you support streaming responses when tool-calls take longer? We want partial replies while ticketing is created.

[08:05] Diego: We do streaming on Hosted and Dedicated. For tool-calls that are async we typically send an initial suggested reply and later an updated confirmed reply. We'll show a demo of that pattern.

[08:15] Anita: Great. On security docs, our legal asks for data residency proof and API contract — can you share your audit logs schema?

[08:22] Maya: We'll include a sample audit log, retention options, and a redacted API contract. For Private we can give full schema and retention in your environment.

[08:33] Priya: For a pilot, what's the minimal footprint? We want something low-cost to test in parallel with dev.

[08:38] Maya: Hosted pilot: 1–2 dev accounts, managed vector store, a 16k model, sample connectors in webhook mode. For POC we'll provide a checklist to collect sample data. For Dedicated pilot it's a minimum reserved pool — more setup but better parity to production.

[08:55] Marcus: On model updates — if you roll model improvements, can we control rollouts and compare A/B?

[09:00] Diego: Yes — rollouts, canary, A/B testing are supported. You can pin routes to model versions and set automatic fallback on degradation.

[09:10] Anita: Anything we should be careful about before the benchmark?

[09:13] Diego: Make sure prompts represent production, give us examples of failure cases, and include tokenization edge-cases. Bring sample async flows for tool-calls.

[09:20] Maya: OK let's recap next steps. We'll send security docs, Diego will propose benchmark configs, Marcus will share sample data. Plan to reconvene for a 2-hour SE deep-dive next week.

[09:31] Anita: Sounds good. Thanks both.

[09:33] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional mislabels (Speaker 2 instead of Diego), some words transcribed imperfectly ("KVcash" instead of KV cache), and pauses/crosstalk removed for readability.
